# ReaScratch — Pitch-locked audio and video scratching in plain REAPER

<!-- Generated by make_manual_pdf.py. To change it, edit manual/ReaScratch_manual_en.md and build again -->

> **The manual is `ReaScratch_manual_en.pdf`.** How to play, every part of the screen, the parameters, controller setup (the preset list), patterns, the load test and more are all there (with screen diagrams; the text can be searched and copied). This README is just the file list, the setup steps and the troubleshooting table taken from it. (`README.md` and `ReaScratch_manual.pdf` are the Japanese edition.)

Turn the jog wheel of a DJ controller (or a rotary encoder or plain knob) to **scratch the audio without changing its pitch**, while **REAPER's video window shows the frame that matches the play position**.

Runs on REAPER 7.x (Windows / macOS) alone. The basic features need no extensions and no separate FFmpeg install (for what some features such as the LOAD button use, see “What you need” under “Setup”).

---

## Files in the kit

| Folder / file | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Effects/ReaScratch/reascratch.jsfx` | The scratch audio engine (JSFX plug-in) |
| `Effects/ReaScratch/reascratch_cue.jsfx` | The headphone mix (on the `Cue` track; the `Cue mix` knob blends cue and main. The metronome is added wherever the `Cue mix` knob is) |
| `Effects/ReaScratch/reascratch_perf.jsfx` | The performance lanes (`DJ performance lanes`). Setup puts it on each deck's engine track; it records what you do on the deck onto REAPER's timeline while REAPER records, and plays it back in performance playback mode (see “Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline”) |
| `Effects/ReaScratch/reascratch_logo.png` | Title logo of the plug-in screen (keep it in the same folder as the JSFX; without it, plain text is shown) |
| The other images in `Effects/ReaScratch/` (`tex_front.png`, `knob_big.png`, `platter.png` and the other `*.png`) | Images for the plug-in screen (frame, panels, knobs, lamps, switches, TBKgao logo mark, record, help watermark). Keep them in the same folder as the JSFX. It works without them, but with a simpler look |
| `Effects/ReaScratch/LICENSE_Saike_filters.txt` | License (MIT) of the DJ filter models in the JSFX, ported from Saike's JSFX (Joep Vanlier) |
| `Effects/ReaScratch/LICENSE_ntsc_zhuker.txt` | License (Apache 2.0) of the VHS video effect, ported from zhuker's ntsc |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_setup.lua` | Initial setup: creates the tracks, loads the JSFX and registers the other scripts |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_import_video.lua` | Imports a video. Places it, extracts a WAV (with FFmpeg if available, otherwise with REAPER itself) and loads it into the JSFX. Warns you if the extracted audio goes silent from some point to the end |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_reencode_mjpeg.lua` | Re-encodes a video to all-intra (AVI/MJPEG) and swaps it in (FFmpeg if available, otherwise REAPER itself) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_video_sync.lua` | Syncs the video window to the scratch position. While it runs, it immediately stops REAPER's own play and pause (to keep the picture and sound from drifting apart; recording is not stopped). Run it again to stop it. If you answer Yes in setup, it starts automatically with REAPER |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_video_reopen.lua` | Reopens the video window (use it when the video window has frozen after a monitor or projector was switched off/on or unplugged; fullscreen is kept) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_load_test.lua` | Load test (about 40 s). Each deck scratches by itself while the script measures dropouts, JSFX load and screen stalls, and saves the result to a text file. See “Testing on a low-spec PC (load test)” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_pattern.lua` | Places a scratch pattern on a deck (as envelope automation items). See “Scratching from envelopes (patterns)” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_pattern_save.lua` | Saves a pattern you rearranged under a name and adds it to the pattern menu |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_record_lanes.lua` | Turns writing recorded performance movements into envelopes on or off (on by default). See “Recording a performance into envelopes” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_take.lua` | Turns performance capture on/off (each deck's audio and video, and the finished mix as seen on screen). See “Capturing a performance” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_perf_play.lua` | Turns performance playback mode (`PERF PLAY` on the toolbar) on/off. While it is on, REAPER's playback plays the performance lanes back. See “Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_perf_play_decks.lua` | Chooses which decks performance playback mode plays (both, deck A only or deck B only) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_export.lua` | Write the hot cues, memory cues, CUE, BPM, beat grid and key of the decks' samples to an XML for rekordbox or to ReaScratch track data. See “Writing out track data” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_rekordbox.lua` | Choose the XML exported from rekordbox, Traktor's `collection.nml` or VirtualDJ's `database.xml` and load its hot cues, memory cues, BPM, beat grid and key into the samples. See “Loading cues from rekordbox” |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_patterns.lua` | The included scratch patterns (baby, chirp, tear, flare, crab, transformer, stutter, freeze and more; not run directly) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_deck_mix.eel` | Video processor code that layers deck B's picture over deck A's. Setup installs it in the Video processor on the `video` track (no need to open it) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_lib.lua` | Shared library for the scripts (not run directly) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_browser.lua` | Loads the file chosen in the Media Explorer into a deck with the LOAD button (on controllers that have one), loads files dragged onto a deck's JSFX window, and previews with the `P` key. Called by the sync script, so not run directly. The LOAD button needs the js_ReaScriptAPI extension and the preview needs js_ReaScriptAPI and SWS; loading by dragging needs no extension |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_black.png` | A black picture placed where a sample slot is empty (emptied, or nothing loaded yet), so the video window does not keep showing the last picture. Used by the scripts |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_audio_only.avi` | The spinning speaker video placed where a sample has sound only (it turns with the record. Used by the scripts) |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_lights_off.ps1` | A small program that turns every controller light off after REAPER closes (Windows). It starts with the video sync script and waits for REAPER to close |
| `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_ctl_presets.lua` | Writes and reads controller presets made on the setup screen's `Learn` tab (called by the sync script; not run directly). Saved to `Data/ReaScratch_controllers/` in the REAPER resource folder (`<controller name>.reascratch-preset`) |
| `ProjectTemplates/ReaScratch.RPP` | A project template that is already set up |
| `Data/ReaScratch/reascratch_screenset.ini` | The ReaScratch window layout (a REAPER window set). Setup adds it to REAPER's window sets when you answer Yes to "Use the ReaScratch window layout?" |
| `Data/ReaScratch_samples/` | Where the WAVs read by the JSFX are stored (the import script writes them). The `(empty).wav` marks an empty sample slot (a silent file; if you delete it, setup or import recreates it). `rs_load_a1.wav` to `rs_load_b8.wav` hold the sound loaded with the LOAD button (setup makes them), and files such as `rs_load_a1_src.txt` record which source each sound was made from |

## Setup

### What you need

- **REAPER 7.x** (Windows / macOS; tested with 7.80)
- **A MIDI controller** (you can also try it with the mouse and keyboard). Some controllers need the manufacturer's driver.
  - Reloop Buddy (Windows): needs Reloop's “ASIO Driver”. Without it, the jog and buttons do not respond (see “Troubleshooting”).
  - Some Hercules models, CDJs and others: noted under “Preparation” in the table and in “Notes by model” of the “Preset list”.
  - NI Traktor Kontrol (HID): uses the included `HID bridge` and loopMIDI (see “HID controllers”).
- **Used when present** (the basic features work without them)
  - FFmpeg: importing a video and converting it to all-intra use it so that the frames match the source exactly; capturing a performance also makes videos with it. For where ReaScratch looks for it, see “Heavy video”.
  - The js_ReaScriptAPI extension (install it with ReaPack) and FFmpeg: needed for the LOAD button (loading from the Media Explorer). The LOAD button works on Windows only.
  - The js_ReaScriptAPI and SWS extensions (both from ReaPack): needed for previewing a Media Explorer file (the `P` key).
  - FFmpeg: needed for loading a file by dragging it onto a JSFX window (js_ReaScriptAPI is not needed). Like the LOAD button, it works on Windows only.

### 1. Copy the files

You can install with ReaPack or copy the kit's folders by hand. Use one of the two.

**With ReaPack** (you can also get updates via ReaPack)

1. In REAPER, choose `Extensions` > `ReaPack` > `Import repositories...`, paste this URL and click `OK`:
   `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tobokegao/ReaScratch/main/index.xml`
2. In `Extensions` > `ReaPack` > `Browse packages...`, find `ReaScratch`, right-click it, choose `Install`, then click `Apply`.
3. The installed files and their locations are the same as when copied by hand. The manual PDFs and the HID bridge are not included; get them from the GitHub Releases if you need them.
4. Restart REAPER and proceed to "2. Initial setup".

**By hand**

1. Connect your MIDI controller to the PC and start REAPER.
2. In REAPER, choose `Options` > `Show REAPER resource path in explorer/finder`. This opens the **REAPER resource folder** where plug-ins and scripts live (it contains folders such as `Effects` and `Scripts`).
3. Copy the kit's **`Effects` / `Scripts` / `Data` / `ProjectTemplates`** folders into that folder as they are (merging with the folders of the same name).
   - **macOS note**: dragging onto a folder of the same name in Finder "replaces" it by default, deleting what was already in `Scripts` and the others. **Hold Option while dragging and choose "Merge"** (if "Merge" does not appear, open each of the 4 folders and copy their contents into the matching folders).
4. Restart REAPER.

### 2. Initial setup

1. Open `Options` > `Preferences` > `Audio` > `MIDI Inputs` and check that your controller's MIDI input is enabled (Enabled).
   - To light the controller's buttons, also enable the same controller under `MIDI Outputs`. Setup points the deck tracks' MIDI output there (if you enable it later, run setup again; see “Button lights”).
2. Open `Actions` > `Show action list...`.
3. Click `New action...` > `Load ReaScript...`, load `Scripts/ReaScratch/reascratch_setup.lua`, select it in the list and click `Run`.
   - If you installed with ReaPack, `reascratch_setup.lua` is already in the list: type `reascratch_setup` in the filter box, select it and click `Run`.
   - First (after checking that the JSFX is installed), a menu “Language / 言語 (ReaScratch messages)” appears with three choices: `Auto (follows REAPER's language pack: …)` (the end shows the language Auto gives right now), `English` and `日本語`. The current setting is checked. `Auto` gives Japanese when the filename of the language pack chosen in REAPER (`langpack=` under `[REAPER]` in reaper.ini) is a Japanese one (it contains `Japanese`, `jpn` or `日本`, or starts with `ja_`, `jp_` and the like), and English otherwise (also when no language pack is used). Closing the menu without choosing keeps the current setting. The setting is stored in REAPER on this PC (for all projects); the rest of this setup run and the messages of the other scripts use it. The menu appears every time you run setup.
   - Three tracks, `video`, `audio` and `scratch engine`, are created, and the JSFX is inserted on `scratch engine`.
   - The MIDI input of `scratch engine` is set to "All MIDI inputs". You choose your controller with the JSFX's `Preset` (see below).
   - The other scripts are registered in the action list too (search for "`reascratch`" to find them).
   - You are asked “Make a second deck (deck B)?”. Yes creates 4 tracks, `video B`, `audio B` (both muted), `scratch engine B` (deck B's JSFX) and `video B view` (shows deck B's picture; just above or just below `video`, to suit the project's video settings), plus a Video processor on the `video` track that layers the two pictures. If you answer No, the answer is stored in the project and you are not asked again for that project (to add deck B later, create an empty track named `scratch engine B` and run setup). See “Two decks with layered video (deck B)”.
   - A `Cue` track for headphones is created. It is not sent to the master but straight to the headphone output. If an output has "Phones" or similar in its name, that one is used; otherwise a menu “Which output goes to your headphones (Cue)? (to change it later: ROUTE on the Cue track)” lists the outputs and you pick the one your headphones are on (for example `Analog 7 / Analog 8` on an RME Fireface UCX II). The choice is saved in REAPER's settings on this PC and you are not asked again. See “Listening to a deck on headphones (Cue)”.
   - A box titled “ReaScratch setup: video conversion height (smaller = lighter, coarser)” asks for `Height (720 / 540 / 360)` (default 720; another number becomes the nearest of the three). This is the height used when converting videos to all-intra; smaller is lighter on the PC and coarser. Choose 540 or 360 on a slower PC. The value is kept in REAPER's settings on this PC and applies to all projects (Cancel keeps the current value).
   - If REAPER is set to draw the video ahead and cache it (REAPER's default), a notice “REAPER is set to draw the video ahead and cache it.” appears. With this, the crossfader and video effects show up about 0.2–0.5 s late. Right-click the video window (`View` > `Video`) and choose `Performance tweaks (experimental)` > `Video cache` > `All media and video FX are not cached`. It works at once; no need to restart REAPER.
   - Next you are asked “Start the video sync (reascratch_video_sync.lua) automatically when REAPER starts?”. **We recommend Yes.** A few lines are added to REAPER's `Scripts/__startup.lua` (a file REAPER runs every time it starts), and from then on the picture follows automatically as soon as you open a project that contains ReaScratch, without starting the sync script by hand. Projects without ReaScratch are left alone. To stop auto-sync, run setup again and answer No; only the added lines are removed (the rest of `__startup.lua` stays as it was).
   - Then you are asked “Use the ReaScratch window layout?”. Yes puts ReaScratch's 10 buttons on toolbar 3 (SETUP, IMPORT VIDEO, MJPEG, VIDEO SYNC, VIDEO REOPEN, PATTERN, PATTERN SAVE, REC LANES, TAKE, PERF PLAY) and adds a window set “ReaScratch” (this toolbar at the top left, the video window at the top right at 16:9) in a free slot. If toolbar 3 already has other buttons, or window sets #01-#10 are all in use, you are asked before they are replaced (what was there is kept; see “Things that depend on your setup”). REAPER reads window sets when it starts, so **restart REAPER**, then switch with the action `Screenset: Load window set #NN` (NN = the number in the message). The same kind of action switches back to another layout.
4. Open the video window with `View` > `Video`.
5. Choose your controller. Open the JSFX window with the [FX] button of the `scratch engine` track, press `setup` in a bottom corner (usually the bottom right; when you made deck B, deck A's window is mirrored and it is at the bottom left) and pick your model from the `Preset` menu (manufacturer → model → `deck 1` / `deck 2`; see “Preset list”). If you made deck B, pick `deck 2` in the JSFX window of `scratch engine B`. For a controller without a preset, make one in setup's `Learn` tab (see “Check by touch / make a preset”). Without a controller, `Custom` is fine.

> **Tip: new projects from now on**
> Once setup has been run, you can start straight from `File` > `Project templates` > `ReaScratch` (the template only contains deck A's `scratch engine`; deck B, the `Cue` track and the controller's button lights (the MIDI output) are created and set when you run setup after opening the template).

### ReaScratch buttons (toolbar 3)

If you answer Yes to the window layout prompt, the following 10 buttons appear at the top left of the window set “ReaScratch” (it is REAPER's toolbar 3; with another layout, open it with the action `Toolbar: Open/close toolbar 3`). Each button does the same as running the script of the same name from the action list.

| Button | Script it runs | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `SETUP` | `reascratch_setup.lua` | The initial setup (the steps on this page). You can run it any number of times (to add deck B or the `Cue` track, re-point the MIDI output, change the message language, and so on) |
| `IMPORT VIDEO` | `reascratch_import_video.lua` | Imports a video as a sample (“Step 1: Import a video”) |
| `MJPEG` | `reascratch_reencode_mjpeg.lua` | Converts a video to all-intra (AVI/MJPEG) and swaps it in. It converts the selected video items, or the video of deck A's current sample when nothing is selected (“Heavy video”) |
| `VIDEO SYNC` | `reascratch_video_sync.lua` | Starts / stops the video sync (each press toggles it; “Step 2: Start the sync”) |
| `VIDEO REOPEN` | `reascratch_video_reopen.lua` | Reopens a video window that has stopped (“Projector output”) |
| `PATTERN` | `reascratch_pattern.lua` | Places a scratch pattern on a deck (“Placing a pattern”) |
| `PATTERN SAVE` | `reascratch_pattern_save.lua` | Saves a rearranged pattern under a name (“Saving a rearranged pattern”) |
| `REC LANES` | `reascratch_record_lanes.lua` | Switches whether the performance being recorded is written to envelopes. The button is lit while on (on by default; “Recording a performance into envelopes”) |
| `TAKE` | `reascratch_take.lua` | Turns performance capturing on / off. The button is lit while on (“Capturing a performance”) |
| `PERF PLAY` | `reascratch_perf_play.lua` | Turns “play the performance” on / off. The button is lit while on (“Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline”) |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **No sound** | Monitoring settings / no file loaded | - Check that record arm (red circle) and input monitoring (speaker) are ON for the `scratch engine` track.<br>- Check that the JSFX window's waveform view shows a waveform (if it says "no sample", run the import).<br>- If `Untouched transport` is `Stop`, there is no sound while you are not touching the jog. |
| **The sound stops 0.15 s after the knob stops** | Touch mode setting | - With a touch sensor: set `Touch note` to the right note number (54 on the FLX4).<br>- Without a touch sensor: this is normal. To keep sounding while stopped, set `Auto release` to `0` (stop it with the `Release note` button). |
| **Pressing the jog does not scratch (touch does not work)** | The controller's jog mode | On controllers with a VINYL (scratch) mode switch, check that it is ON (when OFF, some controllers do not send the top touch, and the jog acts as a pitch nudge). If the JSFX's `touch` lamp lights when you press the top, the touch is arriving |
| **Silence after reaching the end** | End-of-sample setting | With `At end of sample` set to `Stop (silent)`, reaching the end with your hand off gives silence (if you are touching the jog, the last grain keeps sounding so you can pull back). To keep playing from the start, change it to `Loop to start`. |
| **The video window froze after a projector/monitor was switched off/on or unplugged** | REAPER's video window stopped drawing | Run `reascratch_video_reopen.lua` to reopen the video window (see “Projector output”) |
| **The picture does not follow** | The sync script is not running | - Check that `reascratch_video_sync.lua` is running (it toggles, so running it again stops it; even with auto-sync chosen in setup, running it once by hand stops it).<br>- Check that the video window is open with `View` > `Video`. |
| **Opening `ReaScratch-HID-Bridge.exe` or a `.command` shows a warning and it will not start** | Windows / macOS block unsigned programs | See “If a warning stops it from starting” under “HID controllers (NI Traktor Kontrol S4, S3, S2)” |
| **The crossfader and video effects show up late in the picture** | REAPER draws video ahead and buffers it | Right-click the video window → `Performance tweaks (experimental)` → `Video cache` → `All media and video FX are not cached`. It takes effect immediately (setup also tells you if it is not set) |
| **Video seeking is jerky** | Keyframes are far apart | The video is still compressed H.264 or similar. Convert it to MJPEG as described in “Heavy video (all-intra conversion)”. |
| **The sound drops out / crackles** | Too much load on the PC | Measure as described in “Testing on a low-spec PC (load test)”. A larger audio buffer, a smaller video height in setup, or closing other background software helps. |
| **The imported audio goes silent partway through** | An old version of the video sync script | A warning appears on import. An old version of the video sync script stopped playback while REAPER was rendering. Update the kit to the latest version and import the video again. |
| **Playback stops partway through the track / the waveform is cut off** | The track is too long | If the waveform view shows "only the first ○:○○ of ○:○○ loaded" in red, the track exceeds the length that can be loaded. Cut the video shorter and import it again. |
| **Turning the Reloop Buddy does nothing (Windows)** | The MIDI driver is not working | With the standard Windows driver, the Buddy's MIDI part (jog and buttons) does not start ("Code 10" in Device Manager). Install the "ASIO Driver" from the Reloop product page and reconnect the Buddy (how to check: below the table). No driver is needed on a Mac. |
| **With two decks, deck B's picture is not layered / breaks up when stopped / video effects do not work on B** | The project's video settings | This does not happen in projects made from the kit's template (`File` > `Project templates` > `ReaScratch`). In the current project, run `reascratch_setup.lua` again (it moves the `video B view` track to the place that suits the project's video settings; restarting the video sync does the same). If that does not help, close REAPER, open the project file (.rpp) in a text editor, delete the one line starting with `VIDEO_CONFIG`, save, and open it again (the cause is below the table). |
| **The JSFX cannot be found** | Files in the wrong place | Check that `Effects/ReaScratch/reascratch.jsfx` is inside the `Effects` folder of the REAPER resource folder (the folder opened by `Options` > `Show REAPER resource path in explorer/finder`). |

**Turning the Reloop Buddy does nothing**: Once `Reloop Buddy In` appears in REAPER's `Options` > `Preferences` > `Audio` > `MIDI Inputs`, it is ready.

**With two decks, deck B's picture is not layered** (cause): Depending on REAPER's video settings (`Video` in `Project settings`), the picture of an upper track covers the lower one. Setup and the video sync put `video B view` in the place that suits them, but when the tracks have been reordered by hand, for example, the `video B view` track's picture can be shown as is, hiding the processing that layers the two pictures (the Video processor on the `video` track).

---

## Tested environment

- **OS / host**: Windows 11 / REAPER 7.80 (AVI/MJPEG writing and playback checked without FFmpeg)
- **Test hardware**: Akai APC40 mkII (real hardware), Reloop Buddy (MIDI mapping checked on real hardware; Windows needs the driver), Pioneer DDJ-FLX4 (tested on real hardware only early in development, not with current features (channel faders, headphone CUE button, tempo fader direction and so on); treated as untested like the other models until it is tested again), AlphaTheta DDJ-FLX2 (settings based on the official MIDI message list; not yet tested on the real hardware)
- **Other controllers**: not tested on the real hardware, including the NI Traktor Kontrol models connected over HID (marked as untested in the “Preset list”).
- **macOS**: an early version (2026-10-03) was checked on macOS (REAPER 7.47) by a test user. Features added since (deck B, video blending, the HID bridge and so on) have not been checked on macOS. Linux has not been tried. If something goes wrong, please let us know.

## License & credits

ReaScratch is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). Some parts are code ported from other licenses: the DJ filter (Saike FM Filter 2, MIT License, `Effects/ReaScratch/LICENSE_Saike_filters.txt`), the VHS video (zhuker/ntsc, Apache License 2.0, `Effects/ReaScratch/LICENSE_ntsc_zhuker.txt`), the key detection (libKeyFinder, GPL-3.0-or-later) and the loudness measurement for auto gain (libebur128, Jan Kokemüller, MIT License, https://github.com/jiixyj/libebur128; its K-weighting filter constants and gating are written in Lua as libebur128 does them). The licenses of the parts in the HID bridge's exe are in `HID bridge/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt`. The references and thanks are in `CREDITS.md`.
